questions.q: What is a “highlight” in the Make Time method?
a: One important, meaningful or joyful activity given real time each day
The single most urgent email waiting in your inbox
A reward you earn only after finishing every task
The longest uninterrupted block of work in your calendar
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines the highlight as a daily activity worth 60 to 90 minutes that matters to you.

questions.q: Which two forces does the book blame for stealing our time?
a: The Busy Bandwagon of work and the Infinity Pools of entertainment
Social obligations and the pressure to exercise daily
Poor planning and an inability to say no to family
Financial stress and the need to work a second job
questions.why: Lesson 2 names the Busy Bandwagon of work and Infinity Pools of entertainment as the two big time wasters.

questions.q: What do the authors say is needed beyond willpower to stay focused?
a: Redesigning your environment to reduce distractions
Setting stricter deadlines for every task
Working longer hours until the habit forms
Removing all technology from your home
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that willpower is not enough and that you must change your surroundings.

questions.q: Why does the summary recommend adding caveman-style activities to your day?
a: Our bodies are out of sync with modern sedentary life
They burn more calories than any gym workout
They help you disconnect from friends and family
They replace the need for a consistent sleep schedule
questions.why: Lesson 3 explains that human bodies evolved long before farming and sedentary living, so small primal habits restore energy.

questions.q: Which change does the summary suggest for handling the news?
a: Check it once a week instead of several times a day
Read only the headlines and never the articles
Turn on notifications so you never miss an update
Cancel every news subscription permanently
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists checking the news weekly rather than many times a day as a way to cut distraction.
